claims.text: Toughness retention in refractory high-entropy alloys is governed by competition between irradiation- or thermal-driven defect recombination and grain-boundary segregation followed by brittle precipitation.
The initial W-Ta-Cr-V refractory HEA is single phase.
The initial W-Ta-Cr-V refractory HEA has a nanocrystalline or ultrafine-grained microstructure.
The initial alloy has a homogeneous elemental distribution and no pre-existing precipitates.
W-Ta-Cr-V can be irradiated at approximately 1073 K to approximately 8 dpa.
A W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf alloy can be tested under high-temperature irradiation conditions near the proposed dose range.
A minor Hf addition is expected to mitigate grain-boundary segregation in W-Ta-Cr-V.
The relevant W-Ta-Cr-V and W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf samples can be prepared as magnetron-sputtered thin films.
Cr-V-rich nanoscale grain-boundary clusters or precipitates form and can embrittle the HEA.
Severe lattice distortion in HEAs produces similar vacancy and interstitial mobilities.
Similar vacancy and interstitial mobilities enhance defect recombination.
Enhanced defect recombination preserves a homogeneous microstructure and toughness.
Beyond a critical irradiation dose or thermal exposure, increased defect mobility drives localized elemental segregation at grain boundaries.
Grain-boundary segregation nucleates and grows brittle precipitates.
The proposed brittle precipitates reduce resistance to crack propagation.
Hf stabilizes grain-boundary composition and counteracts segregation.
The baseline alloy maintains high toughness up to a threshold irradiation dose and loses toughness when grain-boundary precipitates appear beyond that threshold.
The Hf-modified alloy exhibits delayed or reduced precipitate formation relative to the baseline.
The Hf-modified alloy retains higher toughness than the baseline under matched irradiation conditions.
The proposed behavior applies to nanocrystalline or ultrafine-grained refractory HEAs from room temperature to approximately 1073 K and from 0 to roughly 8-10 dpa.
